clue.text: Athletes who get the highest value petrol annoyed with Shell initially

indicators.note: annoyed suggests something stirred up and agitated, so the letters of value petrol are jumbled
initially points to the opening letter of the word Shell

explanation.surface: Top-scoring athletes are irritated by the price of fuel at the Shell garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annoyed' rearranges VALUE PETROL into POLEVAULTER; 'initially' adds the S from Shell.
explanation.definitionFit: In their event these competitors clear a bar set higher than in any other jumping discipline, so they reach the greatest heights.

clue.text: Meaty food — this might go on one's crumpet

definitions.meaning: a British pastry filled with chopped pork

definitions.text: this might go on one's crumpet
definitions.meaning: crumpet is British slang for the head

explanation.walkthrough: A crumpet is a British griddle cake, which suggests something spread on it, but here it is slang for the head; a pork pie hat sits on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a savoury pastry snack and a style of hat with a flat circular crown.

clue.text: Actress, say, removing soft coat

indicators.note: removing says the soft letter is taken away from the performer word

parts.note: an actress is an example of a player on stage
P is piano, the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: An actress takes off her soft coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat of paint is a single layer of it spread over a surface, so the two nouns match.

clue.text: Natives in small settlement train slave girl

indicators.note: to train is to shape or form, so the letters of slave girl are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: People from a hamlet are schooling a girl kept in slavery.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who live in a village, a small rural community, are its inhabitants or natives.

clue.text: In jail, guard picked up something to eat

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the hidden letters are lifted and read upwards, backwards
In says the answer sits inside the words jail, guard

explanation.surface: A prison warder collected his meal in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo hybrid, so it is a thing one can eat.

clue.text: Tense about a certain prize

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
re means about or concerning
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone feels nervous about winning a guaranteed award.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to value it highly, the verb sense of prize; as nouns both are precious things too.

clue.text: Journey around grand upland area

indicators.note: around means the journey word goes round the grand letter

parts.note: a ride is a journey
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A trip goes round a magnificent hilly region.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow raised stretch of high ground, a type of elevated terrain.

clue.text: Grilled food from pub — be prompt

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a cue is a prompt, as given to an actor

explanation.surface: Someone at a pub is urged to be on time for the cookout food.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbecue denotes meat cooked over an open grill, and by extension the meal itself.

clue.text: Remained dignified on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio signals what is heard rather than written, a word that sounds the same

parts.note: staid means sober, sedate and dignified

explanation.surface: A broadcaster stayed composed while on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stayed somewhere is to have remained there, the past tense of a synonym.

clue.text: Your label's different colour

indicators.note: different says the letters of your label are to be made into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone's tag is a different shade from yours.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a named deep, bright shade of blue, so it is an example of a colour.

clue.text: Large number following daughter's plan

indicators.note: following places the large-number word after the daughter's letter

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
a raft of things is a large number of them

explanation.surface: A daughter's scheme comes after a big count of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline, i.e. a scheme sketched out before it is finalised.

clue.text: Father pulled back locks, revealing outcast

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: pulled back says the word for locks is drawn the other way, read backwards

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: A dad tugs his hair back and turns out to be shunned by society.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah is a person rejected and avoided by everyone, a social reject.

clue.text: Fool European maiden by holding large meeting

parts.note: an ass is a fool
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: holding means the word by keeps the large letter within it

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: An idiot from Europe keeps a young woman by him at a big gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly is a gathering of people convened together, so it is a synonym for a meeting.

clue.text: Hard interrupting Italian novelist, editor reflected

indicators.note: interrupting means the hard letter breaks into the novelist's name

parts.note: Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist, author of The Name of the Rose
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough interruption of Umberto Eco by his editor was thought over.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflected sound or light is thrown back, as an echo bounces sound back, so echoed is a synonym.

clue.text: Thumping worker a bit

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as a farmhand
some means a bit, an amount

explanation.surface: A labourer is doing a bit of hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome win or profit is a large one, just as a thumping victory is a very big one.

clue.text: Egg on sandwiches Mussolini, perhaps, made

indicators.note: sandwiches means the urging word encloses the leader's title like bread round a filling

parts.note: to egg someone on is to prod or urge them
Mussolini was Il Duce, the leader; perhaps marks him as one example of a duce

explanation.surface: Urging someone on, eggs in sandwiches were what Mussolini cooked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To have produced something is to have created or manufactured it, a synonym of made.

clue.text: Edward put up with endorsing planning

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the name is raised so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Ed is short for Edward
endorsing a cheque or document is signing it

explanation.surface: Edward tolerated the backing of a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Designing and planning both mean working out how something is to be made or done.

clue.text: Many think about summit on Everest, primarily

indicators.note: about means the thinking word goes round the summit word

parts.note: to mull is to think something over
a tip is a top or summit

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word Everest

explanation.surface: Many think about reaching the top of Everest first of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiple and many are both adjectives describing a large number of things, as in multiple or many injuries.

clue.text: Old fogey ruins a do, dancing

indicators.note: dancing has the letters of ruins a do moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A stuffy old man spoils a party by dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinosaur is figuratively a person with outdated views who resists change, just like an old fogey.

clue.text: Want expensive article reduced

parts.note: dear means costly or expensive

indicators.note: reduced means the article loses its last letter, cut short

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A wish for a costly item that has been marked down.
explanation.definitionFit: Want as a noun means lack or shortage, which is what a dearth is.

clue.text: Feature a page penned by religious school

indicators.note: penned by means the page letter is shut inside the religious school word as if in a pen

parts.note: a sect is a religious group or school of thought

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature page is written by a religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is one particular part or characteristic of something, a synonym of feature as a noun.

clue.text: Cast's regularly seen in that place

definitions.text: Cast's regularly seen in that place

indicators.note: seen in means the picked letters appear inside the word for that place

parts.note: there means in or at that place

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word cast's

explanation.surface: The acting company is regularly found at that venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes A and T, the 2nd and 4th letters of CAST'S. The whole clue also defines: a play's cast is regularly seen there.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is the venue where actors perform, so a play's company appears there night after night.

clue.text: Utter lies about drunk? Not I!

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of lies about are reeling about into a new order
Not I says that the letter I is excluded from the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A drinker denies being drunk and tells complete lies about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles LIES ABOUT; 'Not I!' drops one I from those letters before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter and absolute are both adjectives meaning complete or total, as in an utter or absolute disaster.

clue.text: Loaded gun's first removed from convict hideout

indicators.note: removed from means that letter is taken out of the convict and hideout words

parts.note: lag is British slang for a convict, as in old lag

indicators.note: first selects the opening letter of the word gun's

parts.note: a den is a hideout

explanation.surface: A criminal's lair has had its loaded gun taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means carrying a heavy load, so it is a synonym of loaded, as in a laden or loaded truck.

clue.text: Some bigwig no reporters disregard

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A VIP with no journalists present gets overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to take no notice of it, which is what disregard means as a verb.

clue.text: Old vessel crossing eastern body of water

indicators.note: crossing means the vessel word spans across the eastern letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a can is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: An ancient ship traverses an eastern sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is one of the very large expanses of sea covering most of the earth.

clue.text: Sounds like the fellow will get better

indicators.note: Sounds like says the answer is a word pronounced the same as the phrase

parts.note: the fellow will, shortened, is he'll

explanation.surface: It seems the man is going to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: To heal is to recover from injury or illness, so the verb matches the phrase about recovering.

clue.text: This writer is one day behind rear of coconut shy

indicators.note: behind places the setter's words, one and day after the coconut's end letter
rear of points to the last letter of the word coconut

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as this writer, so this writer is becomes I'M
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: The setter spends a day at the back of a fairground coconut shy.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where people throw balls to knock coconuts off stands; 'shy' looks part of that scene but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shy and timid are synonymous adjectives describing someone nervous and lacking confidence.

clue.text: Ford maybe parking next to hotel guest

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
a resident is a guest staying at a hotel

explanation.surface: A Ford car is parked beside a hotel guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' looks like the carmaker but means Gerald Ford, 38th US President; 'maybe' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Ford held the top office in the United States, so he is one example of a head of state of that title.

clue.text: Telling niece about secret enemy information?

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of telling niece are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone passes on to their niece some hidden intelligence about the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: In military and spying language, intelligence is gathered knowledge about an adversary, often covert; the question mark flags the definition by example.
